title: 6.0 Power Stroke: oil cooler, EGR cooler, head gaskets, FICM
summary: The famous ones all connect: a clogged oil cooler kills the EGR cooler, and overheating/pressure pushes head gaskets with the stock torque-to-yield bolts.
steps: Check the oil cooler first: compare engine oil temp (EOT) to coolant temp (ECT) on a scan tool at full warm-up under load. A spread over about 15 F points to a clogged oil cooler.
Check for EGR cooler failure: white smoke on startup, coolant loss with no visible leak, coolant in the intake.
Head gasket test: pressure in the degas bottle, coolant pushed out under load, bubbles in the degas tank.
FICM: hard start/rough running when cold; check FICM output voltage (should be about 48 V while cranking).
Permanent fix most shops sell: head studs and new gaskets, upgraded oil and EGR coolers, a new FICM if weak, plus a coolant filter.
